title: Till Computation Note: The Credit Put Toward a New Piece
content:
The credit put toward a new piece under the Belrose Trade-In and Upgrade Programmes is the credit the registration shows as issued, taken at the share the desk lets go on one sale, which is sixty percent (60 percent).

## The calculation

1. **The share.** The credit the registration shows as issued is taken at 60 percent and the figure is rounded to two decimal places.
2. **Held back.** Nothing is held back against the window in which the traded piece may still be taken back.
3. **Spending above the least the customer must spend.** Nothing is added for spending above the least the customer must spend. The price of the new piece is read as the least the customer must spend that the registration records.
4. **The result.** The share is taken first and rounded to two decimal places, what is added for spending above the least the customer must spend is rounded to two decimal places on its own, what is held back is then taken off, the figure is not taken below nothing, and the result is rounded to two decimal places at that final step only.

Of the entries booked to a registration, an entry moves the credit where it books the credit, revalues it upward, spends it or takes it away; a valuation entry and an inspection entry move nothing, whatever amount they carry.

## Worked through on hypothetical figures

A registration shows 7000.00 USD issued, and its entries carry the credit booked at 7000 USD and nothing else that moves the credit.

| Quantity | Figure (USD) |
|---|---|
| credit still available | 7000.00 |
| share of it at 60 percent | 4200.00 |
| added for spending above the least the customer must spend | 0.00 |
| held back | 0.00 |
| credit put toward the new piece | 4200.00 |

On a registration showing 950.50 USD issued, the share at 60 percent is 570.30 USD, and that is the credit put toward the new piece.
